name: Green Sea Turtle
ecologicalRole: Herbivore and seagrass meadow keeper, helping maintain healthy coastal ecosystems.
funFacts: Green sea turtles can travel thousands of miles to return to the same beaches where they were born.
Despite their name, their shells are usually brown, while the green comes from the fat under their shell.
habitat: Warm, shallow coastal waters with seagrass beds and coral reefs.

name: Clownfish
ecologicalRole: Symbiotic partner with sea anemones and small reef-scale nutrient recycler.
funFacts: Clownfish are immune to the stinging cells of sea anemones thanks to a protective mucus layer.
All clownfish are born male; the dominant fish in each group becomes female.
habitat: Warm coral reef lagoons and sheltered reef slopes.

name: Pufferfish
ecologicalRole: Algae and invertebrate grazer, helping control reef growth and nutrient balance.
funFacts: Pufferfish can inflate their bodies with water to appear much larger when threatened.
Many pufferfish contain tetrodotoxin, a powerful toxin that makes them dangerous to predators.
habitat: Shallow reef flats, seagrass beds, and sandy lagoons.

name: Octopus
ecologicalRole: Intelligent predator and scavenger that helps maintain balanced reef food webs.
funFacts: Octopuses can change skin texture and color instantly for camouflage and communication.
They are among the most intelligent invertebrates with excellent problem-solving skills.
habitat: Rocky reef crevices, underwater caves, and coral reef shelters.

name: Coral Reef
ecologicalRole: Foundation habitat provider supporting a quarter of all marine species.
funFacts: Corals are animals that live in symbiosis with photosynthetic algae called zooxanthellae.
Healthy coral reefs grow only a few centimeters per year but form massive structures over thousands of years.
habitat: Warm, clear, shallow waters of tropical seas.

name: Jellyfish
ecologicalRole: Open-water drifter and predator of plankton with a role in nutrient cycling.
funFacts: Jellyfish do not have brains, bones, or hearts, yet many species travel long distances.
Some jellyfish are bioluminescent and glow in the dark ocean at night.
habitat: Open ocean and coastal waters, often near the surface.

name: Whale
ecologicalRole: Ocean giants that help regulate marine food chains and nutrient cycles.
funFacts: Many whales use low-frequency songs to communicate across vast ocean distances.
When whales dive and surface, they move nutrients through the water column and support plankton growth.
habitat: Open ocean, from surface waters to deep offshore zones.

name: Shark
ecologicalRole: Apex predator that maintains healthy fish populations by removing weak or sick individuals.
funFacts: Sharks have been living in the ocean for more than 400 million years.
Some sharks can detect a single drop of blood in the water from hundreds of meters away.
habitat: Coastal reefs, open ocean, and deep sea environments.

name: Stingray
ecologicalRole: Bottom-dwelling predator that helps control populations of crustaceans and small fish.
funFacts: Stingrays use electroreceptors on their snouts to locate hidden prey in the sand.
Their flattened bodies allow them to glide gently along the seafloor.
habitat: Sandy flats, reef edges, and shallow bays.
